task.title: Preserve explicit Human/Ops reviewer assignments through fallback
task.phase: Supervisor governance / protected reviewer preservation / operator V8

observed_failure.head: 7b268b468ca9cd619481fb8bc6a95ac663ac9cd4
observed_failure.root_cause: Assignment planning required every reviewer to be an auto-dispatchable worker and helper claims preferred the old owner over the explicit reviewer. Human/Ops is an external governance actor, so normalization and helper/owner fallback could silently replace that gate while trying to form an eligible worker pair.

scope.owned_layer: Supervisor assignment-pair planning, Human/Ops reviewer preservation, exact-head review-approved normalization, reassignment persistence guard, and focused regressions.
scope.not_changing: Account identity, quota groups, provider configuration, fallback ordering for non-Human/Ops agents, ai-status command semantics, canonical runtime state, live services, deployment, product tasks, or PR #4508 source.
scope.task_brief_history: empty; the supervisor-generated untracked worktree brief is context only and is not part of the delivery range

contract.explicit_gate: A canonical reviewer value equal to Human/Ops is an explicit external governance gate, not an unavailable auto-worker lane.
contract.pair_planning: Owner normalization, helper claim, and owner-failure recovery may still select a viable owner, but Human/Ops remains the only reviewer candidate for that task.
contract.reviewer_failure: A purported Human/Ops reviewer-worker failure cannot invoke reviewer fallback; the task remains awaiting the explicit human gate.
contract.review_approved: When an explicit Human/Ops approval is bound to a complete PR/head/base identity, mainline normalization changes neither owner nor reviewer and awaits governed closeout.
contract.unbound_owner_recovery: An unbound review-approved task may retain existing owner recovery, but the Human/Ops reviewer is preserved.
contract.persistence_guard: Supervisor reassignment persistence rejects any attempt to replace an incumbent Human/Ops reviewer. Intentional operator reassignment remains available through governed ai-status commands, whose semantics are unchanged.
contract.atomicity: Owner recovery still persists owner, reviewer, and status with exact expected owner/reviewer/status compare-and-swap under the canonical task-state lock.
contract.identity_boundary: No account or quota equivalence is inferred. Codex and Codex2 remain distinct configured identities, and non-Human/Ops fallback traversal is unchanged.

concurrent_stale_compare_and_swap.result: Two concurrent callers form plans from owner=Codex/reviewer=Human/Ops; Codex2 wins once, Claude's stale plan is rejected, and the reviewer remains Human/Ops.

tests: .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py tests selected by pair_planner, normalize_mainline_task_assignment, helper_claim, and persist_task_reassignment
